lessons: Don't use StreamReader.readline() for stdout: the default 64 KiB limit raises ValueError on long stream-json lines. Read in chunks (e.g. read(65536)), capture every byte, split lines from a carried partial buffer, and flush the tail at EOF.
Add a test_seams case with a stdout line over 64 KiB, run with and without a callback, and assert the returned capture is byte-identical.

Send every exception that escapes the capture block (callback raise, reader error) through _kill_and_wait before re-raising, e.g. `except BaseException: await _kill_and_wait(proc); raise`. Test that a raising callback leaves no live child group.

Strengthen the dormancy test in test_watchdog.py: scan the squatch/ package and assert no production module except providers.py references on_event, on_stdout_line or EventCollector. Or drive the production call path and assert no callback keyword reaches the process.
The provider-side normalization, the flat-estimate start event and the no-consumer kwargs pin passed review. Keep them and change only the seam read loop, the exception path and the tests.
reason: Checks passed. Review found fixable oversights (64 KiB readline limit, kill path skipped on non-timeout exceptions, weak dormancy test), and each finding comes with a concrete fix.
